title.narrative: Up-skilling Ukrainian humanitarians in trauma-informed approaches (NGORC component)

description.narrative:
Please note, this project is carried out as part of a consortium with Depaul, the NGO Resource Centre, and Christian Aid with their partner APH. CAFOD will hold the primary relationship with the DEC and will transfer funds separetely to Depaul,the NGORC, and Christian Aid.
Ukrainian civil society has stepped up to the challenge of providing millions of people with humanitarian assistance over the last 2 years. Thousands of ‘accidental humanitarians’ with very limited background, experience or expertise have demonstrated huge commitment, applying their experience and skills from other sectors to providing assistance and services for vulnerable, at-risk and trauma-affected people. Many staff and volunteers have been and continue to be affected by the war personally, and there is a significant need for mental health and psychosocial support activities while maintaining staff well-being and preventing burn-out.
As the humanitarian response evolves into a protracted crisis, there is a need to support local and national actor (L/NA) staff to develop sustainable approaches to providing humanitarian assistance across the country in the medium-long term. An investment in skills training to further strengthen Ukrainian civil society in person-centred and trauma-informed approaches to supporting vulnerable, at-risk and trauma-affected people will improve the quality and effectiveness of services and ensure a more sustainable recovery and reconstruction process when the time comes. This increased understanding will also minimise the potential for harm and/or the re-traumatisation of people
